newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares advance strongly over bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares advance strongly over bourse trade.

text.p: German shares ended bourse trade on Thursday strongly ahead, after chalking up solid gains on data which indicated slower than expected economic growth in the first quarter of the year.
Shares were also buoyed by advances in the German bond market. It went ahead after Germany's powerful Bundesbank decided to leave its key interest rates unchanged.
The DAX index ended up 29.80 points at 3,383.25 points, building on a stable start in pre-bourse trade despite sharp declines on car giant Daimler-Benz.
Daimler ended down 3.51 percent, or 4.85 marks, at 133.30 marks after releasing 1996 earnings late on Wednesday.
Dealers said some of Daimler's news, including plans for a convertible note issue, had proved disappointing, especially in the light of the recent rally among German car shares.
But the overall market got a boost from a report showing the Ifo institute's business climate index fell to 92.4 in March from 93.6, far below expectations for a figure of around 94.0.
Volumes were moderate ahead of the Bundesbank's annual news conference to follow its regular policy-making council meeting later on Thursday and before Wall Street's opening.
Shares in BMW ended up 14 marks at 1,431.
BMW chief Bernd Pischetsrieder said on Wedesday that BMW was expecting "slight" earnings growth in 1997, a comment he clarified as meaning single digit percent growth.

Airline Deutsche Lufthansa was little moved by a statement from the company saying its 1997 results would be above those in 1996. Its shares edged 12 pfennigs higher to 22.70 marks, but ended slightly lower, down eight pfennigs at 22.50 marks.
